gloss: dire financial straits; desperate money trouble

definitions.gloss: dire financial straits; desperate money trouble
definitions.explanation: A household or organization whose finances are so strained that it can barely meet its obligations. Nearly always used in the pattern {家計|かけい}は{火|ひ}の{車|くるま}だ.

examples.japanese: うちの{家計|かけい}は{火|ひ}の{車|くるま}だ。
examples.english: Our household finances are in dire straits.

examples.japanese: {売上|うりあげ}が{落|お}ちて、{会社|かいしゃ}は{火|ひ}の{車|くるま}になった。
examples.english: Sales fell and the company ended up in serious financial trouble.

examples.japanese: {外|そと}からは{立派|りっぱ}に{見|み}えるが、{内情|ないじょう}は{火|ひ}の{車|くるま}で、{給料|きゅうりょう}の{支払|しはら}いも{遅|おく}れている。
examples.english: It looks impressive from outside, but internally the finances are desperate and even salaries are being paid late.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
From {火車|かしゃ}, the blazing cart of Buddhist hell said to carry sinners away — hence a state of torment, narrowed in modern use to financial torment.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {家計|かけい}が{火|ひ}の{車|くるま}: the household budget is in crisis
- {内情|ないじょう}は{火|ひ}の{車|くるま}: the real finances are desperate
- {火|ひ}の{車|くるま}になる: to fall into dire straits

USAGE:
Restricted to money. A schedule or workload that is desperately tight is not {火|ひ}の{車|くるま} but {火|ひ}の{回|まわ}りが{早|はや}い or simply {大変|たいへん}.
